items.title: 4.1.3.1 Infix, Postfix, and Prefix Notations; Converting an Infix Expression to Postfix

source_refs.note: Topic 4.1.3.1 with 'Converting an Infix Expression to Postfix' (PDF 97-98, printed 94-95). The prefix example prints as '-\-AB' and 'x' is used for multiplication; the prefix form of (A + B) x C is worked here (general knowledge, flagged). MCQ 4 and long question 4 are answered.

blocks.text: Postfix and prefix need no parentheses to show the order of operations; in + A x B C, B and C are multiplied first and then A is added.
Converting infix to postfix with a stack

items: Start with an empty stack and an empty output list, and read the expression from left to right.
Operand: add it to the output.
Operator: first pop to the output any operator on the stack with higher or equal priority, then push the new operator.
Right parenthesis: pop operators to the output until the left parenthesis, then discard the parenthesis.
At the end, pop all remaining operators to the output.

blocks.text: Example: 3 + 4 * 2. Read 3: output [3]. Read +: stack [+]. Read 4: output [3, 4]. Read *: higher priority than +, so push: stack [+, *]. Read 2: output [3, 4, 2]. End: pop all: 3 4 2 * +.
